messages.subject: overdispersion or zero-inflated dated
parts:
I have completed an opportunistic survey for cetacean sightings over the =
past 2 summers. I have several candidate covariates which I am using to t=
ry and predict density within my study area. They include: latitude,longi=
tude, depth, salinity, SST, and tidal speed. I am in the DSM stage of my =
analysis where I am trying multiple GAM models using these candidate cova=
riates, starting with a saturated model and removing terms to improve fit=
. I have many segments with zero sightings in them, and as such have a ze=
ro-inflated data set. I am worried that this is likely affecting the fit =
of my model because of overdispersion.=20

Does anyone have any suggestions of how to deal with this in Distance. Do=
es this require me to work from R where I can manipulate the model more? =
I have been able to set distance to create the R files but not run the an=
alysis and have thought about trying to manipulate the code in these file=
s? would this be the best strategy?

Thanks
Nicole
